episode.title: Halt repeated variants of read-only repository inspection commands
episode.before: At parent commit 680f523853175856236162460fcd6985c9d68620, the always-on loop detector recognized consecutive calls only when the tool name and complete arguments were identical, plus a per-turn tool-call cap. Variants such as repository status, summary diff, revision-only diff, and tracked-file listing produced different argument hashes, so a consecutive sequence of semantically equivalent read-only inspections could continue without the always-on detector identifying stagnation.
episode.after: At commit 3ce46949c2132dd8b3cc8f05cdc6c023aee0c2da, shell tool requests are classified into a common repository-overview-inspection bucket only when every shell-chain segment is a read-only status, diff, or tracked-file listing and any diff is revision/option based rather than path-specific. Eight consecutive bucketed requests halt the run through the always-on safety tier, record and emit a dedicated loop type, clear pending calls, and expose a human-readable CLI reason. Nonmatching calls and retries reset the streak; session disable is honored; write-bearing, mixed-purpose, non-repository, and file-specific review commands fail open.
episode.diff: The change adds a semantic classifier and consecutive-streak state to the loop-detection service, invokes the new check between the identical-call guard and hard per-turn cap, resets its state at progress/retry/prompt boundaries, introduces a dedicated telemetry enum value, and propagates that reason through the existing client halt path and non-interactive message formatter. It adds regression coverage for variant and newline-separated inspection loops, threshold behavior, reset behavior, session disable, and false-positive exclusions. Five files changed with 461 insertions and 16 deletions.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned commit 3ce46949c2132dd8b3cc8f05cdc6c023aee0c2da resolves the linked issue through PR 5944 and has parent 680f523853175856236162460fcd6985c9d68620; five files changed with 461 insertions and 16 deletions.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 3ce46949c2132dd8b3cc8f05cdc6c023aee0c2da; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0] and manifest_metadata.provenance

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation's always-on tier checked only exact consecutive tool-call identity and the per-turn cap; it had no semantic shell-inspection bucket or streak.
evidence_units.source: git show 680f523853175856236162460fcd6985c9d68620:packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts, checkAlwaysOnSafeties and service state fields

evidence_units.claim: The change introduces an eight-call shell-inspection threshold, a bucket key and streak, classification helpers, detection and logging, and reset integration.

A shell request is bucketed only when its command is a nonempty chain whose every segment is a read-only status, diff, or tracked-file listing; path-specific diffs, write-bearing chains, and mixed commands are excluded.
Matching requests increment one semantic streak and trigger at eight; a nonmatching request clears the bucket and streak, while retry and prompt reset paths also clear the state.

Production streaming invokes the guard before configuration-gated heuristics; on detection it clears pending tool calls, emits LoopDetected with the recorded type, performs error cleanup, and returns the turn.
The new dedicated loop type is part of the telemetry contract and the non-interactive CLI maps it to a human-readable reason and identifies it as outside the model.skipLoopDetection gate.
Regression tests prove that eight distinct and compound/newline-separated read-only inspection variants trigger the always-on guard, set the dedicated loop type, and log its telemetry value.
Regression tests prove that a non-inspection tool request or retry resets the inspection streak and that an explicit session disable prevents this detector from firing.
Boundary tests prove that write-bearing repository chains, chains containing another command type, non-repository shell commands, and file-specific diffs are not placed in the stagnation bucket.

Validation is grounded in the committed regression suite, but the tests were not rerun in this checkout because the working tree currently presents tracked files as deleted and the runtime executable is unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: classify-read-only-overview-inspections
candidate_atomics.title: Classify only non-progressing overview inspections
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize syntactically varied shell requests into one stagnation class only when every command segment performs repository-wide read-only inspection, while treating productive or narrowly targeted commands as progress.

semantic_action.intent: Recognize repeated operations that are semantically equivalent despite argument variation without misclassifying productive shell work.
semantic_action.pre_state: A shell tool request contains an unclassified command string that may have multiple chained segments.
semantic_action.post_state: The request has either one stable overview-inspection key or no stagnation key; write-bearing, mixed-purpose, non-repository, and path-specific review commands have no key.
semantic_action.validation: Feed positive command variants and negative boundary cases through the always-on checker; only complete chains of overview-style read-only inspections may contribute to the common streak.

candidate_atomics.name: halt-consecutive-semantic-stagnation
candidate_atomics.title: Stop a consecutive semantic inspection loop
candidate_atomics.description: Track consecutive requests sharing the semantic inspection key, reset on progress or replay boundaries, and halt at the bounded threshold while respecting the explicit session override.

semantic_action.intent: Bound a loop whose tool arguments vary while its observable read-only operation remains unchanged.
semantic_action.pre_state: No loop has fired, detection is enabled for the session, and incoming tool requests may repeatedly map to the same semantic inspection key.
semantic_action.post_state: At the threshold the loop is marked detected with a dedicated reason and logged; before the threshold processing continues, while nonmatching calls, retries, and prompt resets clear the streak.
semantic_action.validation: Verify no detection through threshold minus one, detection and telemetry at the threshold, streak restart after nonmatching calls and retries, and suppression after session disable.

candidate_atomics.name: propagate-structured-halt-reason
candidate_atomics.title: Propagate the structured halt reason to consumers
candidate_atomics.description: Carry the newly detected reason through telemetry, stream termination, pending-call cleanup, and user-facing reporting so consumers observe a consistent contract.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure a detector firing produces an actionable, consistently typed halt rather than allowing queued work to continue or reporting an ambiguous failure.
semantic_action.pre_state: The always-on detector has returned true and recorded the semantic stagnation loop type while pending tool requests may exist.
semantic_action.post_state: Pending requests are discarded, a typed loop event is emitted, the turn terminates through the existing cleanup path, telemetry can distinguish the reason, and headless output explains the halt and configuration behavior.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the production call site and reporting mappings to confirm the same loop type drives cleanup, stream output, telemetry, and the human-readable message.

candidate_workflows.name: bound-semantic-tool-call-stagnation
candidate_workflows.title: Add a precise circuit breaker for argument-varying tool stagnation
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for detecting repeated tool requests that differ textually but share one non-progressing semantic operation, while preserving productive variants and propagating a structured halt contract.

workflow_graph.goal: Halt a bounded run of semantically equivalent, non-progressing tool requests even when their raw arguments vary, without stopping productive or targeted operations.
when_to_use: A tool loop evades exact request equality because the model rewrites arguments while repeating the same observable read-only operation.
The repeated operation has a narrow semantic class with evidence-backed exclusions precise enough for an always-on or high-confidence guard.
The runtime already has a termination path capable of discarding queued calls and emitting a structured reason.
anti_goals: Do not classify all repeated uses of one tool name as equivalent.
Do not stop write-bearing, mixed-purpose, targeted-review, or otherwise progress-bearing operations merely because they contain an inspection segment.
Do not place the new precise guard behind a broad heuristic-skip setting when the intended contract is always-on, though an explicit session-level disable may remain honored.
Do not alter unrelated content, thought, read-file, alternating-call, or hard-cap detectors.
not_applicable_when: No stable semantic equivalence class can be derived from the structured request or command payload.
The suspected loop includes productive state changes or target-specific narrowing that constitutes progress.
Only issue-title or similarity evidence exists without an implementation diff and validation oracle.
The consumer has no safe halt path for cancelling queued operations and reporting the reason.
inputs: Counterexamples that must count as progress
Structured tool name and argument payload
Retry, prompt-reset, and session-disable lifecycle semantics
Typed loop-event, telemetry, and user-message contracts
workflow_graph.entry_state: Exact request equality does not catch a repeated semantic operation because each consecutive request varies its arguments, so the run can continue until a distant generic cap or external failure.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Only the proven non-progressing request class shares a semantic key; its uninterrupted streak halts at the configured bound, progress and replay boundaries reset it, excluded operations continue, and all consumers receive one structured halt reason.

steps.condition: Use only after positive loop variants and productive counterexamples establish a narrow semantic boundary.
steps.validation: Positive overview-inspection variants share one key, while write-bearing, mixed, non-repository, and path-specific cases do not.

steps.condition: Apply when consecutive requests receive the admitted semantic key and detection is not explicitly disabled for the session.
steps.validation: The threshold request fires; threshold-minus-one does not; nonmatching requests, retries, and prompt resets restart counting.

steps.condition: Apply whenever the new circuit breaker reports detection.
steps.validation: The production stream clears pending calls, emits the dedicated reason, terminates, logs telemetry, and provides a matching user-facing explanation.

validation_ladder: Classifier unit boundary: admit distinct overview-style read-only variants and reject productive, mixed-purpose, unrelated, and targeted operations.
State-machine boundary: verify threshold-minus-one, exact threshold, interruption reset, retry reset, prompt reset, and explicit session disable.
Integration boundary: confirm the guard executes before configuration-gated heuristics and clears queued requests on detection.
Contract boundary: confirm one dedicated reason is consistent across detector state, emitted stream event, telemetry, and user-facing text.
Repository validation: run the focused loop-detection test file in a clean checkout with the repository's declared runtime and package manager.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if semantic equivalence cannot be expressed narrowly enough to avoid known productive cases.
Stop if the detector cannot reset on observable progress or replay boundaries.
Stop if a firing cannot safely cancel pending requests and terminate the current run.
Do not claim runtime validation until the focused tests execute successfully in a usable checkout.
